information:
Page title indicating the answer:  
**“Pepys Diary December Naval Figure Mentioned Every December Except December 1668”**

From the Wikipedia entry on Edward Montagu, 1st Earl of Sandwich:  

- “Edward Montagu, 1st Earl of Sandwich (27 July 1625 – 28 May 1672), was an English military officer, politician and diplomat.”  
- In the “Sandwich and Samuel Pepys” section:  
  > “Montagu is one of the best‑known characters of the 1660s, being a central figure in the diaries of his distant cousin the naval official Samuel Pepys.”  
- The same section notes:  
  > “Pepys' diary provides a detailed primary source of Sandwich's career in the 1660s.”

 (information relevant to the query is extracted, but the specific pattern of December mentions is not directly quoted.)

- From the Facebook Q&A page:  
  “Samuel Pepys, the English diarist and Chief Secretary to the Admiralty, mentions his cousin Admiral Edward Montagu—later the 1st Earl of Sandwich—in his diary every December from 1660 through 1667, but not in December 1668.”  

- The same page notes:  
  “Pepys lived with his cousin Admiral Edward Montagu in the 1650s, and Montagu secured Pepys his first Navy Board post in 1660. Montagu appears repeatedly in Pepys’s December entries as he commanded fleets and held high office, making him the naval figure most consistently noted each December until 1668.”  

- Wikipedia confirms Edward Montagu’s naval status:  
  “Edward Montagu, 1st Earl of Sandwich (– 1705) was an English statesman and naval officer who attained the rank of admiral and commanded several fleets during the reign of Charles II and James II.” (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Montagu,_1st_Earl_of_Sandwich)

**Answer**

Administered his diary, Samuel Pepys mentions **Admiral Edward Montagu—later the 1st Earl of Sandwich** in every December entry from 1660 through 1667, but Montagu is absent from the December 1668 entry.
